mainTopic: The extra verse that gives each kind of קדשים its own לאו, and why רבא counts only five lashings for a זר who eats an עולה outside the wall before זריקה
overview: The גמרא first explains that the separate prohibitions for eating קדשים outside the wall come from an extra verse in דברים 12:17, not from a קל וחומר. The תורה already listed these offerings earlier, so spelling each one out again gives each its own לאו. Then the גמרא returns to רבא's ruling: according to רבי שמעון, a זר who eats from an עולה before זריקה outside the wall gets five sets of lashes. The גמרא asks why he is not also lashed for the ban on a זר eating holy food. It answers that this ban only covers food that כהנים may eat, and no one eats an עולה. It then asks about the ban on holy meat that left its boundary. It answers that this ban only covers meat that may be eaten inside, which again leaves out an עולה. Finally the גמרא suggests a third possible lashing, based on רבי אליעזר's reading of ״לֹא יֵאָכֵל כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הוּא״, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse in דברים 12:17 is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier difficulty by saying the extra prohibitions come from a verse that would otherwise be unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is an extra verse. The תורה already listed all the offerings that must be eaten in the chosen place. It could have just said 'You may not eat them' in general. Why does it go back and spell out each one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to where the separate prohibitions come from: an extra verse. It shows the verse is extra by asking why the תורה lists each item again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא was bothered that we cannot give lashes based on a קל וחומר alone. Now it shows that the verse in דברים 12:17 repeats a list the תורה already gave. A short general ban would have been enough, so the long list must be there to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra verse, one that seems unneeded and so teaches something new
After all; since we already know
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Why do I need it?

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'why do I need it?' is not a challenge against the answer. It is part of the answer: it proves the verse is extra.

phrases.english: Rather, it is an extra verse.
phrases.notes: He means the verse in דברים 12:17: 'You may not eat within your gates…'

phrases.english: After all, it is written:
"And you shall bring there… and you shall eat
before the Lord your God in the place, etc."
Let the Merciful One write: "You may not eat them,"
so that the Merciful One goes back and spells them out one by one,
why do I need that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the earlier problem that lashes cannot be given from a קל וחומר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a verbal source (an extra verse) in place of a logical derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra prohibitions seemed to rest only on a קל וחומר, and we do not give lashes based on that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibitions come from the extra wording of דברים 12:17.

steps.title: A separate prohibition for each item
steps.stepSummary: The repeated list is there to give each item its own separate לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the list is there to give each and every item its own separate prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer: the long list in the verse makes a separate prohibition for each kind of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because each item is named on its own, each one gets its own לאו. That means one who eats one item can be lashed for that item's own prohibition. The source is now a verse, not a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: To single out; to give something its own separate status
Prohibitions (negative commandments) that can bring lashes
For each and every one

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, the separate prohibitions for eating קדשים outside the wall come from the extra list in דברים 12:17, so lashes can be given for them.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to give them separate prohibitions,
to each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְיַחוֹדֵי לְהוּ לָאוֵי לְכׇל חַד וְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why do I need it' of step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each item in the list of דברים 12:17 has its own separate לאו.

steps.title: רבא: a זר who eats an עולה gets five sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבא's ruling about a זר who ate from an עולה before זריקה outside the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point. רבא said: a non-כהן who ate from an עולה before its blood was sprinkled, outside the wall, gets five sets of lashes according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבא's statement so it can look at it more closely. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has several features at once: the eater is a זר, the offering is an עולה, the blood was not yet sprinkled, and he ate outside the wall. רבא counts five separate לאוין according to רבי שמעון, who counts separately each prohibition discussed earlier. The next steps ask whether even more lashes should be added, starting with the fact that he is a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself; returning to a statement quoted earlier
A non-כהן
A burnt-offering, which is burned completely and eaten by no one
Sprinkling the blood of an offering on the מזבח
Outside the wall (of ירושלים)
Receives lashes

phrases.english: Back to the matter itself. רבא said:
A non-priest who ate from a burnt-offering
before the sprinkling, outside the wall,
according to רבי שמעון, receives five sets of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a statement of רבא quoted earlier and starts a new discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a זר who eats an עולה before זריקה outside the wall receives five sets of lashes.

steps.title: Why not a sixth lashing for a זר eating קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he is not also lashed for the ban on a זר eating holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him also be lashed for the verse 'And a non-כהן may not eat, for they are holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's count: the eater is a זר, so the ban on a זר eating holy food should add more lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known לאו that forbids a זר from eating קדשים. Since the person here is a זר eating קדשים, it looks like this לאו should add to the five.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him also be lashed
Holy; sacred food

phrases.english: But let him also be lashed because of:
"And a non-priest may not eat, for they are holy"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of five in רבא's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's count of five sets of lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eater is a זר eating holy food, so the לאו of 'וזר לא יאכל' should add another set of lashes.

steps.title: The זר ban only covers food fit for כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The ban on a זר eating only applies to food that כהנים are allowed to eat, and an עולה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule only applies where the food is fit for כהנים. Here, it is not fit even for כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the ban on a זר eating is only for holy food that כהנים may eat, so it does not apply to an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban for a זר is about separating him from the כהנים who may eat. An עולה is burned completely and no one eats it, not even a כהן. So there is nothing special about the eater being a זר, and there is no extra lashing.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only…; this rule is limited to…
Fit; allowed to be used or eaten

phrases.english: That applies only where it is fit for priests;
here, it is not fit for priests either.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any זר who eats any קדשים is lashed for 'וזר לא יאכל'.
steps.terutzMaskana: That לאו applies only to food that כהנים may eat, which leaves out an עולה.

steps.title: Why not lashes for meat outside its boundary?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he is not also lashed for the ban on eating holy meat that left its proper area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him also be lashed for the verse 'Meat torn in the field you shall not eat.' Once meat goes out of its boundary, it becomes forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge: the meat was taken outside its proper area, and there is a לאו against eating such meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the field' are read to teach that holy meat which leaves its boundary becomes forbidden. This meat is outside the wall, so it seems that this לאו should add another set of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn; here, meat that became forbidden
In the field; read as 'outside its proper place'
A boundary or partition
Becomes forbidden

phrases.english: But let him also be lashed because of
"And meat torn in the field you shall not eat,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30. 'In the field' is read as meat that's outside its proper place.

phrases.english: meaning: once meat has gone out of its boundary,
it becomes forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִילְקֵי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם ״וּבָשָׂר בַּשָּׂדֶה טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the count of five, built the same way as step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's count of five sets of lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The meat left its boundary, and 'ובשר בשדה טרפה' forbids such meat, so this should add another set of lashes.

steps.title: The boundary ban only covers meat that may be eaten inside
steps.stepSummary: The ban on meat leaving its boundary only applies to meat that may be eaten inside, and an עולה may not be eaten even inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule only applies where the meat is fit to be eaten inside. Here, it is not fit even inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way as the first: the boundary ban does not apply to an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the boundary only makes a difference for meat that may be eaten inside. An עולה may not be eaten inside either, so going out does not change its status. This ban does not add a lashing.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside (within the proper holy area)
Here, in our case
Also not; not either

steps.whatToRemember: Both extra לאוין ('וזר לא יאכל' and 'ובשר בשדה טרפה') apply only to meat that is allowed to someone somewhere. An עולה is eaten by no one, so they do not add lashes. So far רבא's count of five stands, but the next step tries a third possible lashing.

phrases.english: That applies only where it is fit to be eaten inside;
here, it is not fit inside either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6, built the same way as the answer in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any holy meat that leaves its boundary is forbidden by 'ובשר בשדה טרפה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: That לאו applies only to meat that may be eaten inside, which leaves out an עולה.

steps.title: Should he also be lashed based on רבי אליעזר's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the person is not also lashed for the ban that רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק ״לֹא יֵאָכֵל כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הוּא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him also be lashed according to רבי אליעזר. For רבי אליעזר said: "It shall not be eaten because it is holy"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a third possible extra lashing for the person who ate the עולה. It starts quoting רבי אליעזר's teaching on a פסוק, and the full explanation comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 4–7 the גמרא turned down two extra lashes because neither ban fits an עולה. Now it points to a different ban, taken from the פסוק ״לֹא יֵאָכֵל כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הוּא״ as רבי אליעזר reads it. The question is whether this ban also applies here and adds lashes. That would go against רבא, who did not list it.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with, following someone's view (as in כִּדְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר)
It shall not be eaten. This is the wording of a לאו (a negative commandment).

phrases.english: And let him also be lashed in accordance with רבי אליעזר,
as רבי אליעזר said:
"It shall not be eaten because it is holy",
phrases.notes: שמות 29:34. רבי אליעזר's explanation of this פסוק continues in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second suggested lashing was turned down in Step 7, the גמרא tries a third ban that might add lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling (Step 3) about how many lashes the זר gets for eating an עולה outside the wall before זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר's reading of ״לֹא יֵאָכֵל כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הוּא״ makes eating holy food that may not be eaten a lashable לאו, this case should get that lashing too, and רבא left it out.
